subject: Re: MAP update — proposed three-stage rebaseline and risk heat-check
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@enterpriseco.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: MAP update — delivery timeline slip and options

Hi Priyom / Grace,

Quick update from our side after the product acceptance run yesterday: the evaluation uncovered two integration items that will push our cutover by at least three weeks unless we take a staged approach. Our internal PMs are asking for: (1) a short, negotiable rebaseline for the full rollout, or (2) a phased go-live where core user groups pilot the feature while fixes are applied.

As you know, the original MAP (v2) assumed a single Go-Live on Sept 15. We attached a redlined MAP (v3) with the items we flagged — see attached. Can Redwood provide a concrete staged plan, which components we can canary first, and whether there are fallbacks we can accept without losing the acceptance window?

Short asks for your team:
- Confirm whether we can do a two-week canary for the embeddings service only
- List which deliverables would remain in scope for Sept 15 vs deferred
- Any changes to SLA or pricing if the final cut is delayed

Attaching: EnterpriseCo_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Director, Platform Integrations
EnterpriseCo
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP update — delivery timeline slip and options

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We reviewed the attached MAP and did a short risk heat-check internally. High level notes:

1) Feasible two-phase approach: canary embeddings first (10% traffic) then tiered expansion once the KV-caching patch is validated. That isolates the highest cost/token path and gives you early telemetry.
2) Sept 15 partial acceptance: we can scope a "core API" acceptance that includes generation and embeddings for non-legacy models; remaining integration (legacy token mapping & audit hooks) would be deferred to Phase 2.
3) SLAs/pricing: pricing stays under the existing proposal for Phase 1; Phase 2 adds an incremental implementation fee if we provide additional dedicated engineering hours during the roll.

Proposed three-stage rebaseline (attached as comments in v3):
- Stage A (canary): Aug 25–Sep 8 — 10% traffic, monitor latency/cost, enable auto-fallback to model variant B
- Stage B (expanded pilot): Sep 9–Sep 22 — 50% traffic, complete KV cache fix, run SOC2 logging validation
- Stage C (full cut): Sep 23–Oct 6 — 100% traffic, post-cut monitoring window

We also suggest a formal escalation / exec alignment on Sep 10 if any stage is delayed >3 days.

Next steps: Grace will own the operational runbook and Karthik will scope the engineering buffer. Samantha — can you confirm internal stakeholder buy-in for the staged acceptance and whether your procurement team needs a formal amendment? If yes, we'll push a short SOW addendum to DocuSign.

Attachments: EnterpriseCo_MAP_v3.xlsx (updated with staged plan)

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior AE, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Baker <tbaker@enterpriseco.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP update — delivery timeline slip and options

Thanks Priyom — this looks reasonable and closer to what our PMs were expecting. A couple of clarifying items: 

- For Stage A canary, what metrics will you commit to report daily? We need latency P50/P95, error rate, and token-cost delta vs. baseline.
- If Stage A shows an issue, how quickly can Redwood pull the traffic back to the hosted model variant? We need a documented rollback window (15 minutes or less).
- Procurement asked whether a two-week partial acceptance (Stage B) would require us to sign an amendment or whether a PO note will suffice.

On the SOC2 items: we have a short evidence checklist attached (SOC2-evidence-req.pdf). If you can confirm which items require customer-supplied evidence vs. Redwood-managed logs, that will speed the audit.

Quoted for context: 
> On Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 11:02 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Proposed three-stage rebaseline (attached as comments in v3):
> > - Stage A (canary): Aug 25–Sep 8 — 10% traffic...
>
We'll aim to get the procurement answer by EOD Friday. If you can circulate a short runbook with the daily metric snapshot and rollback steps, we'll circulate that to our PMs.

— Tom
Tom Baker
Program Manager, Integrations
EnterpriseCo
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MAP update — delivery timeline slip and options (exec awareness)

Priyom / Karthik — forwarding the thread to flag risk. This deal has a mid-Q close profile and the proposed two/three stage plan materially affects revenue recognition timing. Two asks: 

1) Prepare a one-pager (by EOD tomorrow) summarizing the staged plan, committed telemetry, and explicit rollback SLA (we should commit to <=15 minutes for canary pullback). Include a short estimated delta to recognized revenue (finance needs a band).
2) If procurement insists on an amendment that increases legal or data controls scope (SOC2 evidence), patch coverage may require a temporary dedicated engineering block. Get an estimate for 40–80 engineering hours and cost implication.

I'll join the Sep 10 exec alignment checkpoint if we hit any slippage. Mark this high-priority for Q3 bookings cadence.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
